title: Segmented buddy allocator and eviction-clustering for stable KV cache packing
creator: Marina Cortez
description:
Problem: Our current KV cache allocation pattern leads to progressive GPU memory drift under continuous-batching workloads. Small, variable-sized allocations for model KV slices combined with heterogeneous request sequences create many small free holes (internal and external fragmentation) that prevent dense packing. This increases memory pressure and causes unnecessary fallbacks or OOMs on Dedicated nodes.

Goal: Implement a compacting, segmented buddy allocator tailored to KV lifetimes plus an eviction-clustering policy that co-locates short-lived keys into volatile slabs. The target is to reduce fragmentation overhead by at least 30% across representative RLHF and chat workloads while keeping tail latency impact <5% and throughput regressions <2%.

Approach summary:
- Introduce segmented arenas per-sequence-length-range (0-128,129-512,>512) to reduce size-class crossover.
- Use a buddy allocator within each arena with slab boundaries aligned to 4KB and optional sub-slab packing for very small KV entries.
- Add a lightweight background compaction sweep that triggers when free fragmentation in an arena exceeds a threshold (configurable). Sweeps are incremental and yield to inference threads.
- Eviction clustering: annotate incoming requests with a volatility score (based on prefix-hit rate and kv-access entropy) and preferentially allocate volatile keys from pre-reserved volatile slabs which are cheaper to evict/compact.
- Batch-aware placement: during continuous batching, the allocator prefers contiguous slabs for batched requests to reduce cross-slab scatter and improve kernel locality.

We will ship as an opt-in runtime flag initially and run A/B evaluation on dedicated pools.
acceptance_criteria: New allocator integrated behind feature flag and controlled by runtime config
Benchmarked end-to-end on chat + RLHF synthetic traces showing >=30% reduction in wasted GPU memory vs baseline for median case
P99 latency delta <= 5% in production-like load tests
Throughput regression <= 2% across our standard MLPerf-like harness
No increase in OOM incidents on dedicated test clusters during 48h soak
Documentation added to Confluence and runtime flag descriptions updated
steps: Design: finalize arena segmentation sizes and slab/sub-slab thresholds (Marina + Liam)
Prototype: implement segmented buddy allocator in a feature branch; unit tests for coalescing and split correctness
Bench: integrate the allocator with the KV cache component; run microbench for alloc/free patterns derived from production traces
Eviction clustering: add volatility scoring and allocate from volatile slabs for high-volatility keys
Compaction sweeps: implement incremental sweep worker with backoff and yield semantics
Integration test: run continuous-batching harness across sequence-length distributions and measure fragmentation metrics
Rollout: opt-in flag on dedicated pools, monitor memory usage, latency, and fallback rates
Postmortem & tuning: adjust thresholds, slab sizes, and sweep cadence based on telemetry
notes_and_links: Initial perf results (dev cluster): fragmentation down 38% median, GPU util +1.8%, p99 latency +2.6% (see PR CI artifacts)
